title: SOURCE_TARGETS retired: dynamic NEXTVAL name across ALTER SEQUENCE RESTART has no distinct C3 oracle

payload.source_hypothesis: NEXTVAL(?) resolves a sequence only at evaluation time, so an in-flight statement may retain an old sequence object/cache while ALTER SEQUENCE publishes a new definition
source_anchors: pkg/expression/builtin_info.go:1526-1559 runtime sequence-name evaluation and lookup
pkg/table/tables/tables.go:1646-1663 consumes an existing in-memory sequence range without storage
pkg/ddl/sequence.go:265-270 explicitly documents concurrent DML using the old sequence definition during ALTER
analysis: the proposed schedule used ALTER SEQUENCE RESTART WITH 2 while 2 was already allocated or materialized
RESTART itself intentionally moves the durable sequence position backward, so a clean schedule with no in-flight old statement can also return 2
pkg/ddl/sequence.go explicitly accepts old-definition allocation during ALTER and warns values may cease to be consecutive or monotonic
therefore duplicate-key or INSERT IGNORE loss cannot identify dynamic-name MDL omission as the cause
payload.required_to_reopen: a consequence that is impossible under an ordinary completed RESTART control, or a product contract requiring ALTER to invalidate all old sequence caches before success
payload.why_not_execute: the candidate fails the counterfactual consequence gate in source; a live RED would only demonstrate documented RESTART semantics
